newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks inch higher at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks inch higher at open.

text.p: The Australian share market inched cautiously higher at the open on Wednesday as a modicum of bargain hunting after Tuesday's sell-off countered Reserve bank inaction on interest rates.
A further easing in interest rates had been widely anticipated following the central bank's monthly board meeting on Tuesday.
From the opening, the All Ordinaries index added 6.8 points to 2,415.9.
"Tuesday was a bit overdone and you have seen some buyers returning but not in numbers," said a Sydney-based dealer, noting the slight volumes.
"It's all very light on so far."
Miners BHP, up 11 cents to A$17.54 (US$13.42), and CRA, up 17 cents to A$18.45, led the way back, with gains in the others more thinly spread.
"The big miners are stronger but the rest have only put a few cents on," the dealer said.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about five to three, while about 45 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
